sections.title: Habitat and form
sections.text: This perennial rush forms dense clumps and rhizomes in salt marshes, coastal meadows and dune backshores. Its upright stems are usually 30–100 cm tall.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: The stiff, cylindrical, sharp-tipped leaves can reach 40–60 cm long and 1–2 mm wide. Small brownish flowers with six tepals grow in a branched inflorescence; the capsule is about 2.5–3.5 mm long.

sections.title: Uses and cautions
sections.text: The botanical sources consulted do not document a common food use or a particular toxicity. This should not be taken as evidence that the plant is edible.
